discovery: The Rydberg blockade and its use for quantum logic and programmable quantum simulation with neutral-atom arrays

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: Strong dipolar interactions between highly excited Rydberg atoms suppress multiple excitations within a blockade radius. Lukin co-developed this blockade concept (2001) as a route to controlled entanglement. In 2009 Saffman's group and Browaeys with Grangier demonstrated the blockade between two individually trapped atoms, and soon after realised entangling gates. These groups then built reconfigurable optical-tweezer arrays of hundreds of atoms. With them they observed quantum many-body phases and dynamics, including quantum many-body scars and topological spin liquids, and logical qubits with error correction. The theory is clean and quantitative, the experiments test it directly, and the platform turned an elegant piece of atomic physics into one of the leading architectures for quantum simulation and computation. This work connects precise light–matter control with many-body physics and quantum technology, and its influence on the field will last.
